question: Explain the meaning of 'capital asset' under the Income-tax Act, 1961. Which assets are excluded from it?

points.label: General meaning
points.description: Property of any kind held by the assessee, whether or not connected with business or profession.

points.label: Specific inclusions
points.description: Securities held by a Foreign Institutional Investor that invested under SEBI regulations, and certain unit linked insurance policies that do not qualify for exemption, are also capital assets.

points.label: Stock-in-trade excluded
points.description: Stock-in-trade, consumable stores and raw materials held for business or profession are not capital assets.
points.basis: Income-tax Act, 1961, section 2(14), exclusion of stock-in-trade

points.label: Personal effects excluded
points.description: Movable property held for personal use by the assessee or a dependent family member is excluded, but jewellery, archaeological collections, drawings, paintings, sculptures and other works of art remain capital assets.
points.basis: Income-tax Act, 1961, section 2(14), exclusion of personal effects

points.label: Rural agricultural land and gold bonds excluded
points.description: Agricultural land in India in a rural area (as defined by population and distance from municipal limits), and specified gold bonds and deposit certificates under the Gold Monetisation Scheme, are excluded.
points.basis: Income-tax Act, 1961, section 2(14), exclusions for rural agricultural land and specified gold bonds and deposit certificates
